sections.title: Imports and mode type
sections.what: Loads the React tools and defines the two allowed modes, calm and nerd.
sections.why: Limiting the value to two names prevents typing mistakes in mode checks.

sections.name: ModeContextType, ModeContext
sections.title: Shared shape and default
sections.what: Defines what the shared value contains: the mode and the toggle function. Creates the shared container with calm as the starting value and a do-nothing toggle.
sections.why: The default lets components render outside the provider without crashing.
sections.watch_out: A component outside the provider will silently ignore clicks on the toggle.

sections.name: ModeProvider
sections.title: Provider that holds the state
sections.what: Holds the current mode, reads the saved choice after load, and saves and applies each change, including the page root attribute.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the visitor's choice across visits.
sections.watch_out: The saved value is accepted only if it is calm or nerd. Anything else falls back to calm.

sections.name: useMode
sections.title: Hook for reading the mode
sections.what: A small helper that lets any component read the mode and the toggle function.
sections.why: It is shorter than reaching into the shared container directly in every component.

summary: Holds the calm or nerd display setting for the whole site and lets any component read it or switch it.
purpose: Provides one shared switch that controls the site's wording and look.
why: Likely reason: many components show different text by mode. A shared setting avoids passing the mode down through every level.
how: Starts in calm. After the page loads, it reads the saved choice from browser storage and marks the page root with the mode. Each change is saved and applied to the page root.
inputs: The saved mode in browser local storage, and the user's clicks on the toggle.
outputs: The current mode and a toggle function, available to components below the provider. A data attribute on the page root reflects the mode.
risks: The first render shows calm before the saved choice loads, so nerd-mode visitors may see a brief flash. Storage access is not wrapped in error handling, so blocked storage could break the page.
debug: If the mode resets on each reload, check the stored key named site-mode and confirm the provider wraps the page. If components ignore the switch, check that they sit inside the provider.
